images.title: Grow the carpet: multiply by 8
images.purpose: Pictures the one move of the carpet stepper: going from one step to the next multiplies the remaining squares by 8.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Two large squares side by side, left and right of centre, joined by one bold amber arrow carrying the label of the rule. Each square has its step name above and its count below.
images.exact_structure: Left square: a 3 by 3 grid of 9 equal cells, 8 outer cells filled teal #0072B2, centre cell white (1 hole). Right square, same size: a 9 by 9 grid of 81 small cells; the centre 3 by 3 block of 9 cells is white; in each of the other 8 blocks of 3 by 3 cells its centre cell is white; the other 64 cells are filled teal. One bold amber #E69F00 arrow from left square to right square with '× 8' written large on it. Above: 'Step 1' (left), 'Step 2' (right). Below: '8 squares' (left), '64 squares' (right).
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Every remaining square becomes 8 squares at the next step, so the count is multiplied by 8, not increased by 8.
images.description: Pictures the one move of the carpet stepper: going from one step to the next multiplies the remaining squares by 8.
images.context: Concept T2.C4; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Counters the misconception that the count goes 1, 9, 17 by adding 8.

image_decisions.why: A practice concept for the carpet stepper; the image fixes its core rule (multiply by 8) in one simple step.
